chapter: Strings, arrangements and the Shrine band
title: Leading the Shrine Band in 1971-72
summary: DeDroit describes the Shrine Band's refusal of sectional rehearsals, why he quit leading it, and winning a prize in Memphis through discipline.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: would be money. I mean it. Well, nothing against it. In this day and age I'm not leaving my wife

at home at night to go play around in blue lodges. I'm a Shrine and all that. Mason is all right, there's a lot of crap too. But I'd rather stay home so my wife is safe. She's by herself and we live in the damn big house and leave a thousand burglaries. So I'm not coming with you. I don't need any money. But if I'm going to put up with that stuff, I go to the convention. I pay my way and then I play music. For what? Nobody else plays. Are they down to dancing? And we damn fools wept. They're playing. And half the time it was the wrong place. I won a prize in Memphis with two alto saxophones, a tuba, a drummer and three trumpets. I wonder how I saw them. My wife said this to me. She ought to know. Two alto saxes, both of them couldn't blow their nose, a drummer and a tuba, they were all right. Mike Chapler played the trumpet. He still plays like he did four years ago. He played the sugar blues. We played the Billboard March, the sugar blues, and we got a big medal, big prize. And a couple of them. How lousy were the other bands. I was like, oh. But the only thing we had was decorum. I said to these guys, I said, now when you go on that bandstand, you know in uniform, you're all standing at you see. Don't sit down until I give you the seat. They all sit up and they're like this, oh, just now what life happened. They sat down, oh, they're just a discipline, you know what I mean? The other guys are going to strike like a baritone dragon and like that, you know, and knock the music stands down. I believe we wanted it on our department. This thing you can cut all that out.
